summary: All 34 occurrences fit III.1; no new sense or idiom is justified. Aging is intransitive despite l-series Preterit inflection (-li, -lux, -le, -lan and plural forms), and overt l-marked age-bearers occur.

Preterit often supplies a present resultant state. Preterit-wa places aging before another past stage; Infectum includes concessive aging, future nonaging and permanent negation. No Detransitive is inferred from intransitive semantics.
Count examples after selection: Preterit five, Infectum five, Preterit-wa two. Repeated maternal/father speeches and same-verse repetitions do not each need a new example.

Round 1 has already filled Preterit and Infectum to five examples and proposed resolution of the swy III duplication. Do not repeat either the duplicate-entry correction or routine thin-cell proposals.
Preterit masəwli describes a current resultant old age, often offered as a reason for memory difficulty. This pragmatic association does not itself lexicalize forgetfulness.
Bird aging at 1.21/1002 supports the animal participant extension already noted in round 1. No new idiom is inferred from the whole bird-and-tree comparison.
U zawno masəwle does not overtly encode an object meaning me. The machine translation Time has aged me cannot establish a transitive sense.
Confirm whether syw/swy is an editorial root-label variation. Apply any duplicate resolution only to swy III; preserve swy II.
Check plural masuwwe (60/169) beside masulan and masuwalle; no dialectal distribution inferred from isolated spellings.
99/4 has Turoyo lu malko as addressee but the German makes the king speak to his son; verify speaker/reference before using it as a participant example.
Jan 1.46/2026: resolve lu ʕəmro with masəwle; is age the l-marked participant, a temporal expression, or a nonstandard utterance?
Jan 1.46/2058: is u zawno the aging subject or a topic/temporal expression? A causative reading needs independent confirmation.
Jan 2.3/288: confirm expanded masəwwole beside inherited masuwayle; preserve the spelling without inferring dialectal distribution.
Animal speakers (camel, ox) and the vineyard use the same aging meaning as humans; botanical aging/maturation is already attested by the existing gourd example.

Jan confirms intransitive aging with l-series suffixes in masəwla, masəwli, masəwlan and anterior masəwwole. Preserved w is a spelling/form variant of the developed syw paradigm, not a new root or sense.
